topic: A person's invention is already patented by someone else
text: Well now, here I am, tilling the soil just as I've done for nigh on thirty summers, and what do I hear but a tale of a finer sort? A man from the townsfolk came struttin’ through our village with his head held high, talkin’ about some contraption of his—something to harness the wind, or so he says. He was clucking like a hen who just laid her first egg, all puffed up about it. But then, as the ale was pourin’ and the stories were swapin’, out comes the truth. Turns out, this wasn’t no new marvel; it was a notion others had already penned down and sealed away. Yet, there he stood, blushing as red as a ripe tomato, still smiling wide as if he’d tamed a dragon. I reckon it’s not the idea, but the heart behind it that counts. And his heart, well, it’s as full as the moon on a clear summer’s night.
